title: skills: publish an ask-data skill for a client answering business questions over MCP (list_datasets → query_dataset → labelled fallback)
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this seat's chat, 2026-11-17, verbatim: 「同意你的所有建议，开始立专题子卡」. The ruling record is #34659 comment 6940528935.

## Why

A governed metric that the client never reaches governs nothing. Today the procedure for answering a business question over the MCP door (lift the business words, call `list_datasets` with them, answer through `query_dataset` on one match, ask back on several, fall back to the object tools and say so on none, cite `provenance`) is written in two places a client does not reliably read: the `list_datasets` tool description, and the page at `GET /mcp/skill`.

Who acts on this card: the skills lane. Who reads the result: a person who connected Claude Code (or another MCP client) to an ObjectStack app and asks it for a number.

## Evidence (objectstack `a0326b06`, read 2026-11-17)

- No file under `skills/**` names `list_datasets` or `query_dataset`. `skills/objectstack-query` teaches a developer to write ObjectQL in code; `skills/objectstack-ai` teaches building AI features into an app.
- The procedure text lives in `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts:265-291` (`DATASET_TOOL_LINES`), outside `skills/**`.
- The scenario runner's ask client runs in an empty directory with `--allowedTools mcp__app` (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/driver.ts:468-483`), so every ask score on record is a no-skill score.
- Claude Code loads an MCP tool's schema only after it picks the tool. In this seat's pilot on `examples/app-crm`, a client without a skill often answered from `aggregate_records` and never loaded `list_datasets`; with a skill in `.claude/skills/` it took the governed path and labelled its fallbacks. The computed numbers were right either way: the difference is the path and the citation. Scores are with the maintainer, not on this card.
- On a near-miss word (a bare "revenue", 金额) neither arm asked back.

## Scope

- One new published skill under `skills/`, written for a client that answers questions over a live environment through MCP tools. It is not a section of `objectstack-query`, whose reader writes code.
- Its trigger is the user asking for a number, ranking, breakdown, trend or list from the app's data, in any language; not a file glob.
- It carries the branch for a near-miss word: on a zero-match, read the unfiltered catalogue, and when several measures are a plausible reading, ask which is meant and compute nothing yet. This is the premise the maintainer's E2 ruling rests on (#34659 comment 6940528935).
- `evals/` cases for each branch: one match, several matches, near-miss, no metric, data cannot answer, `membersWithheld`.
- File surface: `skills/<new skill>/**`, `skills/README.md` and the generated skill index. Nothing under `packages/`.

## Done when

- The skill is in the catalog and passes the catalog's existing gates.
- The served text in `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` and this skill say the same thing. Making one generate the other is the sibling server card's work; this card must not leave two diverging texts.
- A repeat of the pilot through the scenario runner (sibling devx card) shows the governed path taken on synonym questions and the fallback labelled.

## Starting text

The wording the pilot measured, as a starting point only:

<details><summary>pilot skill text</summary>

````markdown
---
name: objectstack-ask
description: >
  Answer a business question over a live ObjectStack environment through its
  MCP tools (list_datasets, query_dataset, list_objects, describe_object,
  query_records, aggregate_records). Use whenever the user asks for a number,
  a ranking, a breakdown, a trend or a list from the app's data, in any
  language. Do not use for building or changing metadata.
---

# Answering questions over an ObjectStack environment

Follow these steps in order for every question. Do not skip step 1.

## 1. Lift the business words and look for a governed metric

- Pick out the business words of the question: the thing measured ("win rate",
  "营收", "商机数") and the things it is grouped or filtered by ("by stage",
  "按行业", "本季度").
- Call `list_datasets` with those words as `terms`, in the user's own words and
  language. Send the words as the user wrote them. If the user wrote Chinese,
  send the Chinese words; you may add an English rendering as an extra term.
- Read each dataset's `matches`. A word matches only when it equals a member's
  name, label or synonym. Similar is not a match.

## 2. Decide by the matches

| What `matches` shows | What you do |
|:---|:---|
| Exactly one measure matches | Answer with `query_dataset` using that dataset and measure |
| Two or more measures match, or the same word matches members in two datasets | Ask the user which one they mean. List each candidate's label, its dataset's label and its description. Do not pick one |
| Only a dimension matches | That is a grouping, not a number. Look for the measure; if none matches, ask |
| Nothing matches, but the word is a loose form of several listed measures (the catalogue's labels, names or descriptions contain it or its translation: "revenue" against Won Revenue, Annual Revenue, Planned Revenue; "金额" against several amounts) | Ask the user which one they mean. List each candidate's label, its dataset's label and its description. Do not pick one, and do not compute anything yet |
| Nothing matches and no listed measure is a plausible reading | Fall back to step 4, and say in the answer that no governed metric was used |
| `membersWithheld: true` | Say some measures exist that you may not read. Do not say the metric does not exist |

## 3. Compute a governed metric

- `query_dataset({ datasetName, selection })`: `selection.measures`,
  `selection.dimensions` and `selection.runtimeFilter` use the names
  `list_datasets` gave.
- Cite the source from the answer's `provenance` (the dataset label and the
  measure labels). Do not cite from memory.
- Use the measure's `description` to say what the number includes and excludes.
- If `truncated` is true, say the result is partial.

## 4. Fallback: object queries

- `list_objects`, then `describe_object` on the object you will read. Read the
  field list before you filter: a select field is filtered by its option
  `value`, never its label.
- Prefer `aggregate_records` for a count, sum, average or breakdown. Never page
  through `query_records` to add numbers up yourself.
- Start the answer with one line saying it is not from a governed metric
  (非指标口径), and name the object and fields you computed it from.
- If the object you fell back to is a listed dataset's `object`, add one line
  naming that dataset and its measures, so the user can ask for the governed
  figure.

## 5. When the data cannot answer

- If no metric, object or field records what the question needs, say so and
  name what is missing.
- Never fill a gap with an assumed value, and never draw a conclusion from one.

## 6. Writing the answer

- Answer in the user's language.
- Show labels, not machine names or raw option values.
- Every figure comes from a tool answer in this conversation.
- State the filter and the time window you used, in words.
````

</details>
